assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Making the legacy path count as a delivery again makes _delivered_review_record return the predecessor round and promote_review_run_itself refuse nothing, so the None assertion at 217 and the promoted-is-false assertion at 220 redden; the base arm shows exactly this.
Dropping any one of the same_revision (335), review_run_id (338-341) or dispatch-time (342-344) checks lets the mismatched record deliver, so that case's None assertion reddens.
Removing the no-head refusal at recovery_review_acceptance.py:320 makes promote_review_run_itself promote on the legacy round, so the promoted-is-false and reason assertions redden.
Reading the head from the legacy path or the any-head glob instead of the declared path writes the predecessor head onto the ledger row, so the reviewed_head_sha row assertion at 242 reddens.

findings.text: blocking: the landing record states the run-versus-plan review distinction 'is read from _is_run_review_node in recovery_review_subject.py', but at the reviewed head that symbol is defined in reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:81 and is absent from recovery_review_subject.py; a reader following the citation finds nothing, so the artifact that exists to describe the landed code misdirects whoever verifies it.

follow-on: the done-when's fifth bullet requires 'the manifest names each change with its reason' for the two existing tests that moved their record to the head-keyed path, but the manifest lists the gate files and results without naming either test's change or its reason; the reasons survive only in the evidence fragment and the diff.

item_rounds.diff: Read commit by commit against 820d1f1c3; nine files, 492 insertions and 42 deletions, with production change confined to reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py (the four-condition predicate, _is_run_review_node, _declared_head_keyed_record, _review_dispatch_instant) and reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:314-338 (the no-head refusal), the rest being test and fragment updates.
item_rounds.done_when: The done-when names the new test file, tests/test_a_review_run_promotes_itself.py, tests/test_a_delivered_review_ends_its_turn.py, tests/test_a_run_review_cannot_remove_a_siblings_record.py, a base-arm negative control and a literal pytest command; tests/test_a_review_promotes_only_its_own_verdict.py:213-275 exercises the predecessor, three mismatch and no-head cases, gate-base-arm.log records exactly those five FAILED by id at 820d1f1c3, and gate-head-arm.log reports 41 passed at 870b8e31e.
item_rounds.goal: The node goal is to make a run review count as delivered only by a record of the head its own head-keyed write path names; reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:302-345 now accepts such a record only when it sits at the declared .at-<head> path, describes that head, names this run when it carries a review_run_id, and postdates this run's dispatch.
item_rounds.manifest: Read; it names the seven commits, a seven-file gate at 41 passed, and baseline_suite/after_suite receipts whose failure ids reconcile with gate-base-arm.log (the earlier round's placeholder id at manifest.md:16 is gone); it does not itemise the two existing tests' moved record paths with reasons.
item_rounds.write_paths: The dispatch fence grants reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py, reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py, six test files and the evidence fragment; the diff changes only those nine paths and touches recovery_review_dispatch.py not at all, leaving it byte-identical to base as the manifest's follow-on (a) states.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_review_promotes_only_its_own_verdict.py:213-275 fails for the predecessor round and each of the three mismatches, and gate-base-arm.log:178-182 shows all five FAILED at the base product code, so the guard is shown to fire under the reverted change.
justifications.evidence: The seven-file gate and both arm logs exist and reconcile with the done-when, but the manifest does not name each of the two existing tests' changes with its reason as the fifth bullet requires.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:81 and :102 reuse the existing _review_record_subject, review_described_head, same_revision, run_record_times and run_id_dispatch_time owners, and the added names are mechanism descriptions free of plan labels.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:329-345 returns None unless the declared .at-<head> path holds a complete record describing that head after this run's dispatch, so the legacy path and the any-head glob no longer deliver.
justifications.reuse: Each added definition builds on an owner; _is_run_review_node at recovery_review_delivery.py:81 reads the id grammar through round_node_source rather than re-spelling the prefix test, and the docstring names the two candidate owners it declined and why each does not answer the question.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in the diff (reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py, reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py, the six named tests, the fragment) is inside the node's declared write paths and nothing outside them is touched.
